text.p: Malaysia's Asiatic Development Bhd said on Thursday that contributions from its huge property development project in southern Johor state will start in 1997.
"Contributions will be very substantial," Asiatic joint chief executive Baharuddin Musa told reporters after the company's extraordinary general meeting. However, he declined to give further details.

Asiatic is developing a 30 billion ringgit integrated township, spanning 3,244 hectares, in Johor which will comprise a central business district, a high-tech industrial park, over 36,000 residential units, a theme park and a golf course.
Development is expected to span 30 years. The project is undertaken by Asiatic's wholly-owned subsidiary, Asiatic Land Development Sdn Bhd.
At the meeting, Asiatic shareholders approved Asiatic Land's proposed acquisition of 77 lots of vacant land, totalling five acres, which is part of the project from Genting Bhd.
Baharuddin said the group's property activities would become a major revenue earner besides contribution from its plantations, but he could not estimate the contribution ratio.
In the 1995 financial year, property contributed 13.5 million ringgit or 16 percent towards group pre-tax profit of 80.68 million ringgit.
Plantations were the main earner, accounting for 77 percent of the profit.

Baharuddin said over the next 10 years, more than 50 percent of the group's plantation land would be converted into property projects. Asiatic has a total landbank of about 110,000 acres throughout the country, of which 10,000 acres have been approved for property development.

On the group's plantation activities, Baharuddin said Asiatic is looking for cultivation land particularly in the eastern states of Sabah and Sarawak on Borneo island as well as in Indonesia. "We will continue to look for land. There were a lot of offers but nothing concrete yet," he said.
